items.title: Can split in legislature party reflect in political party? Supreme Court asks in Shiv Sena symbol case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday examined whether a split in the legislature wing of a political party could subsequently percolate into its organisation and primary membership. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation while hearing the Uddhav Thackeray faction's challenge to the Election Commission of India (EC) decision recognising the Eknath Shinde-led faction as the "real Shiv Sena" and allotting it the bow and arrow symbol. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana During arguments by Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal for the Thackeray faction, Justice Bagchi observed that while the existence of a split in the political party had to be examined, a fissure could originate in the legislature party and subsequently "percolate into the organisation and the primary membership". Sibal argued that a split in the legislature party could not by itself amount to a split in the political party. He relied on the Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai v. They are part of a wider list of critical medical equipment lying idle across 26 government hospitals in the city, the Court was told. "The situation of Guru Teg Bahadhur Hospital (GTB Hospital) is also quite shocking where there are 400 ventilators and 910 oxygen concentrators which are lying unused. The Bench also noted that the hospital's ECG (electrocardiogram) machine is non-functional, with no other ECG machine mentioned in the report, effectively leaving the hospital without one. items.title: Supreme Court refuses to issue uniform policy against demolition of long-standing properties, asks States to consider
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined to entertain a petition seeking a uniform policy across the country for regularisation and demolition of long-standing unauthorised constructions. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said such issues essentially fall within the policy domain and thus declined the prayer for constitution a court-empowered committee to formulate uniform guidelines on the subject. The Court noted that circumstances vary from State to State and thus different policy frameworks may be needed to deal with facts of each case. "It would be difficult and may not be prudent for this Court to lay down a uniform policy framework to be applied across various States," the Court said. However, the Court said the States and Union Territories may consider the issues raised in the petition filed by Centre for Law and Good Governance for the purpose of formulating or revisiting their existing policies. "We are hopeful that due consideration shall be given to all such issues by the competent authorities," it said. items.summary: The Kerala High Court has set aside the Central government's refusal to renew the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010 (FCRA) registrations of two NGOs over claims that they financially supported protests against the Vizhinjam Port project [ Kerala Social Service Forum v Union of India & anr and connected case ]. Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas delivered the judgement in two petitions filed by the NGOs, Kerala Social Service Forum and Save a Family Plan India. The Court found that there was no material to show that the organisations had funded the protesters. The Court added that even if financial support had been provided to the peaceful protesters, such support could not by itself be treated as use of foreign funds for an undesirable purpose or against public interest under the FCRA. The right to peacefully protest is constitutionally protected, the Court explained. " When the right to protest is constitutionally guaranteed, exercise of such right cannot be labelled as ‘an undesirable purpose’ or against public interest. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday said it will hear a plea flagging disruption of essential services during protests/ strikes. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed that the plea be tagged with another case concerning venues for protests, rallies and gatherings. "When protests are underway, essential services are disrupted. We do not know who is a protester and who is not. Ingress and egress are completely disturbed," the counsel for the petitioner said. "There is already a case pending before us concerning venues for protests, rallies and similar gatherings. Let this petition be tagged with that matter. But tell us, how can we issue a direction of this nature? We will hear the matter," CJI Kant said. A petition is already pending before the top court over the use of Delhi's Jantar Mantar as a site for protests and gatherings. That plea states that Jantar Mantar is no longer a suitable venue for public protests due to safety and logistical concerns.
